title: Which shutter type suits which opening
author: Böss Group
excerpt: Vented, single-skin, wide-span, grille, high-speed and fire shutters answer different problems. Five questions settle which one an opening needs.
body: Six shutter types cover almost every opening, and they are not interchangeable.

Vented slat is the default on a shophouse or a residential frontage: perforations pass light and air with the door shut. Single-skin curtains are rolled from wide sheet with no joint, which keeps dust out and suits a garage or a lock-up. Wide-span slat in 6063-T5 and T6 closes warehouse and factory openings past 8 m, where wind load rather than curtain weight is the governing case.

The three specialist types answer specific problems. Grille shutters keep a shopfront visible when closed. High-speed doors cycle in seconds to hold a temperature or a clean-air boundary. Fire shutters hold a compartment line for a rated period.

Five questions settle the choice, in this order: what the door is protecting, how wide the opening is, how many cycles a day it will run, what has to be true when the power fails, and what the budget is. Answering them in that order tends to produce a door that lasts; answering the last one first tends not to.
